## I.OMI · Omi Conversation → LP Memory

A **thin relay**. All the work (extraction, PII scrub, dedupe, conflict check, write) happens in LP-MCP at `POST /memory/omi/ingest` — see `src/memory/omi-ingest.js` and `sql/101_omi_memory_source.sql`.

**Why n8n is in the path at all:** Omi can only call one URL with one token in the query string. n8n moves that token out of the URL into a header, adds the LP-MCP Bearer credential, and gives Mark a **Retry** button on a failed run.

**Setup after import**
1. Create a **Header Auth** credential named `LP MCP – Omi ingest`: Name `Authorization`, Value `Bearer <OMI_INGEST_TOKEN>`.
2. Select it on the **POST to LP-MCP** node (the field is empty on a fresh import).
3. Activate, then set the Omi conversation webhook to:
   `https://n8n-main-instance-production-981e.up.railway.app/webhook/omi-memory?token=<OMI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN>`

**Executions are saved on failure only.** A successful run holds a transcript in its execution data, so success is saved as `none` on purpose. A failed run keeps everything so it can be retried — retrying is safe, LP-MCP is idempotent on the conversation id.

**Reading a red run:** 401 = the Bearer credential or `OMI_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` is wrong. 403 = the uid is not in `OMI_ALLOWED_UIDS` (the first test always fails here — read the uid out of `claude_memory_validation_log`, check_name `omi:uid_rejected`). 503 = `OMI_INGEST_MODE` is still `off`. 500 = the ingest itself failed; the reason is in `claude_memory_validation_log`, check_name `omi:ingest_failed`.

nodes.name: Omi Webhook
nodes.notes: Omi POSTs the conversation body and passes ?uid= and ?token= in the query string. Nothing downstream of here logs the body.

nodes.name: POST to LP-MCP
nodes.notes: The Authorization header comes from the Header Auth credential 'LP MCP – Omi ingest' — never from this JSON. Omi's own token and uid move out of the URL into headers here, so the secret never reaches an access log. Three tries, 5 s apart: LP-MCP is idempotent on sha256('omi|'+conversation_id), so a retry after a lost response writes nothing twice.

nodes.name: Respond error
nodes.notes: Omi gets a plain failure. The reason is in the n8n execution and in claude_memory_validation_log — never in the response body.
